data.description:
SURFACE: /settings/tasks assignment -> /files (SESSION column) -> bulk export dialog.

WHAT BREAKS: Tasks authored at /settings/tasks and assigned through the speaker picker produce deliverables with no session linkage. The deliverables dashboard shows '- no session attached' for both speakers, including for a speaker who has exactly one session, and an uploaded slides.pdf still reads 'No session - Priya Raman' in the bulk-export dialog. Consequence is functional, not cosmetic: the export dialog's DEFAULT grouping is 'Group files by Session - One folder per session', and it cannot place these files. Fixture tasks in the same table DO carry sessions, so the association exists as a concept and is simply not established on this path.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed at live sha 75b871d94c6f) -- the backend already supports this; the UI path does not use it:
- src/routes/files.queries.ts:162 -> session: task.submission_id ? { id, title } : null   (the SESSION column is driven entirely by task.submission_id)
- src/routes/task-templates.routes.ts:95 -> submission_id: z.string().min(1).nullable().optional()  -- accepted on assignment
- src/routes/task-templates.routes.ts:634-638 -> validated against the conference when supplied
- src/routes/task-templates.routes.ts:647 -> submissionId: body.submission_id ?? null  -- silently null when the UI omits it
So the assignment UI never sends submission_id and the row is created unattached.

FIX SHAPE: offer a session picker in the assignment flow; auto-attach when the speaker has exactly one session; and make grouped export state what it could not place rather than silently dropping it.

SIZE: medium.

PROVENANCE: sbek run 2026-08-12T15-33-34, content-management judgement, defects[0]. Validated by reading live source.
data.title: File-request tasks assigned via the speaker picker lose their session, breaking grouped export

data.body: Premise confirmed and fixed at c5a519b1. Note for the fleet: a git stash push/pop round trip in this repo is unsafe -- the stash stack is shared across all worktrees. Between my push and pop, MRQ-139 pushed a WIP stash, so my pop applied THEIR work into my tree. Repaired: their stash was stored back as a stash entry (they have since recovered it), their files reverted here, my own restored by SHA (git stash apply <sha>) and dropped by verified SHA. Use 'git stash apply <sha>' + 'git stash drop' resolved by SHA, never bare pop.

Validated against a running build (npx vite dev, sha c5a519b1, seeded demo, driven in the c11 browser as the real organizer and speaker personas).

WHAT I SAW:
1. /settings/tasks -> 'Assign to speakers' on Presentation Upload. The new SESSION block rendered under the picker: 'Aarush Selvan — Their only session — Going deep on Gemini Deep Research' (preselected, no human needed) and 'Alex Volkov — 2 sessions — No session' (a select the organizer must answer). Picked Alex's second session, assigned. GET /speaker-tasks: his new row carries sub_are-reasoning-models-better-llm-judges, exactly the pick.
2. The create door: '+ New task' -> 'MRQ-140 Slide check' (Upload a file, due 2027-05-01) assigned to Aarush (1 session, auto) and Beyang Liu (2 sessions, picked 'Building AI Agents with Real ROI in the Enterprise SDLC'). Both rows landed with their session.
3. /files SESSION column: both MRQ-140 rows read their session title. This is the column that showed '- no session attached' in the finding.
4. Uploaded a real slides.pdf as the speaker persona through the actual portal upload path (POST /me/uploads/sign -> PUT -> /me/uploads/{id}/complete). /files went to Uploaded, 1 version, 69 B, session still attached.
5. Bulk export dialog now reads 'slides.pdf — Going deep on Gemini Deep Research · Aarush Selvan' where the finding saw 'No session - Priya Raman'.
6. Generated the grouped ZIP (grouping=session): entries are ['Tue-1600-Metropolitan_Ballroom_Aarush_Selvan/slides.pdf', 'manifest.txt']. The deck is filed under its real session folder rather than an unplaceable bucket.

Tests: tests/integration/api/task-session-link.MRQ-140.test.ts — 6/6 fail at base (verified by reverting the two route files), 6/6 pass with the fix; it also covers the No_Session_<Speaker> export folder for a genuinely unattached deliverable. Plus tests/node/task-session-link-ui.MRQ-140.test.mjs. Full npm test green (487s wall clock on a machine running several agents' suites at once; no failures). Screenshot: artifacts/mrq-140-session-picker.png

Merged to main as 2ec27051 (PR #126, squashed; merged by the operator at 21:08 UTC).

WHAT SHIPPED: assignment now resolves a session PER PERSON — the organizer's explicit pick, then a batch-wide submission_id, then the speaker's own session when they have exactly one. Both doors (create-with-assign_to and assign-existing) share assignmentStatements, so the create form, the row assign panel, and the API all answer the same way. New optional session_assignments field on both bodies; a pick naming a session its speaker is not on is refused 422 before any write, so a bad pick assigns nothing. /task-assignees carries sessions:[{id,title}]. The picker shows one session control per selected speaker: one session preselected and labelled, two or more a select, 'No session' always sayable. Export files a genuinely unattached deliverable under No_Session_<Speaker> instead of sharing Unscheduled_<Speaker> with sessions that exist but are not yet scheduled. No migration.

EVIDENCE: 6 integration tests (fail at base, verified by reverting the two route files) + 4 UI-contract tests; tsc clean; trace:ac pass; CI fast-gate green; browser-driven validation of both doors, the /files SESSION column, a real portal upload, the export dialog label, and a grouped ZIP that placed the deck in Tue-1600-Metropolitan_Ballroom_Aarush_Selvan/. Independent code review PASS (art_01KZVXAKC5VAMRDTV4AYG9J1X8).

LEFT OPEN (reviewer minors, none blocking, all recorded on the PR): batch submission_id still validates only against the conference, not per person; draft/submitted submissions count as attachable (deliberately the same rule the assignee list uses); a stale preselect can 422 with copy that blames the organizer for a pick they did not make.

FLEET NOTE: git stash push/pop is unsafe here — the stash stack is shared across worktrees. A sibling agent's push landed between mine, so my pop applied their work; repaired by storing their stash back and restoring mine by SHA. Use 'git stash apply <sha>' + drop-by-verified-SHA, never bare pop.
